args.body:
DEVIATION REPORT
Corvid Analytics LLC rev B Counter-Draft vs. Northgale Systems MSA Client Form v2
Reconciled Against the Northgale Commercial Contracting Playbook (2026 Ed.), Transfer/Exposure Impact, and Partner (GC) Instructions

Prepared for: Northgale Systems, Inc. (Customer) — Deal Committee
Counsel: Harrow & Vane LLP
Matter: Corvid Analytics MSA — rev B counter-draft (operative)
Engagement instruction letters of 14 July 2026 and 21 July 2026 (Meredith Okafor, GC)

---------------------------------------------------------------------
I. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
---------------------------------------------------------------------
This deviation report reconciles the counterparty's rev B counter-draft of the Northgale client-form Master Services Agreement against (a) the original client-form base (Northgale Systems MSA, v2, execution-ready), (b) the Northgale Commercial Contracting Playbook, 2026 Edition (the "Playbook"), and (c) the quantified transfer/exposure impact at the $85,000 monthly base fee, consistent with the GC's engagement and supplemental instruction letters.

The GC's direction of 14 July 2026 requires every rev B change to be answered with reference to the Playbook stating whether we accept, counter at an approved fallback, or reject, with the specific figures our counter will take. The supplemental direction of 21 July 2026 moved the Deal Committee meeting up to 29 July 2026 and consolidated the escalation analysis into a single board-approval-style package. This report is the deviation analysis under that framework, identifying every deviation and the required approval/escalation.

The operative counter-draft is rev B of 9 July 2026. Corvid's earlier rev A markup was withdrawn on 9 July 2026 and is retained only for negotiation history; it is not part of this analysis.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
II. SUMMARY OF DEVIATIONS
---------------------------------------------------------------------
The counterparty rev B markup introduces eight deviations from the client form v2 base. Each is evaluated below against the Playbook Standard position, the Approved fallback, and the Escalation trigger. Four deviations (Renewal, Suspension, Wind-Down, Service-Credit Cap) are out of policy as marked and must be rejected or escalated; one (Late Interest) exceeds the playbook ceiling; two (Cap Measurement Period, Convenience Notice) fall below the approved fallback floor and require CLO approval; and one (Carve-Out Deletion) requires joint CLO and CFO approval.

Deviation Summary Table
1.  Section 2.2 Renewal period 1-yr -> 2-yr — OUT OF POLICY (no fallback) — CLO approval
2.  Section 4.3 Late interest 1.0% -> 1.5% — ABOVE PLAYBOOK CEILING — Reject (hold at 1.0%)
3.  New Sec 4.4 Suspension (15 days) — OUT OF POLICY — CFO sign-off required; 30-day cure per PB-4
4.  Section 7.2 Convenience notice 30 -> 90 days — ABOVE 45-DAY ESCALATION THRESHOLD — CLO approval
5.  New Sec 7.4 Wind-down (60 days, full-fee comp) — OUT OF POLICY — Reject; counter at 30-day, OOP-only per PB-3
6.  Section 9.1 Cap period 24 -> 12 months — BELOW 18-MONTH FALLBACK FLOOR — CLO approval
7.  Section 9.2 Deletion of gross-negligence carve-out — NON-NEGOTIABLE — joint CLO + CFO approval
8.  Section 11.2 Credit cap 20% -> 10% — OUT OF POLICY (floor 15%) — Reject; counter at 15% fallback floor

---------------------------------------------------------------------
III. TERM-BY-TERM DEVIATION ANALYSIS
---------------------------------------------------------------------

DEVIATION 1 — Section 2.2 (Renewal): 1-year automatic renewal replaced with 2-year renewal periods.
Base (client form v2): Automatic renewal for successive one (1) year periods unless non-renewal notice given at least sixty (60) days before end of term.
Corvid rev B: Successive two (2) year renewal periods. Rationale given: capacity planning for infrastructure dedicated to Northgale workloads.
Playbook PB-1: Standard = automatic renewal in one (1) year periods. Approved fallback: NONE — multi-year renewal periods of any length are OUT OF POLICY and require CLO approval.
Assessment: Deviation is out of policy; there is no approved fallback. A two-year renewal lock commits Customer to the relationship and pricing well beyond each review cycle.
Position: REJECT at the standard one (1) year renewal. Any departure to a multi-year renewal requires express CLO approval and is not recommended without a correlative pricing/commitment concession from Provider.
Approval: CLO (no fallback available).

DEVIATION 2 — Section 4.3 (Late Amounts): late interest increased from 1.0% per month to 1.5% per month.
Base (client form v2): Undisputed late amounts accrue interest at 1.0% per month (or the maximum lawful rate, whichever is lower).
Corvid rev B: 1.5% per month.
Playbook PB-4: Late interest is never above 1.0% per month.
Assessment: The 1.5% figure exceeds the playbook ceiling. There is no approved fallback above 1.0%.
Position: REJECT. Hold at the 1.0% monthly rate (or maximum lawful rate if lower), which is the playbook ceiling.
Approval: None required (reject to standard).

DEVIATION 3 — NEW Section 4.4 (Suspension of Services): Provider may suspend Services if any undisputed invoice remains unpaid fifteen (15) days after its due date.
Base (client form v2): Client form grants Provider NO right to suspend Services for non-payment.
Corvid rev B: Adds a suspension right after fifteen (15) days past due.
Playbook PB-4: Suspension-of-services rights are OUT OF POLICY unless preceded by at least thirty (30) days' written cure notice; any suspension right of any kind requires CFO sign-off.
Assessment: The counterparty's proposed suspension right (i) conflicts with the client-form base of no suspension, (ii) provides only a 15-day cure window (below the 30-day requirement), and (iii) requires CFO sign-off as a matter of policy.
Position: REJECT as drafted. If any suspension right is to be considered, it must provide at least thirty (30) days' written cure notice and remain subject to CFO sign-off. Recommend no suspension right be granted.
Approval: CFO sign-off required for any suspension right.

DEVIATION 4 — Section 7.2 (Termination for Convenience): notice period increased from thirty (30) days to ninety (90) days.
Base (client form v2): Customer may terminate for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice. No wind-down period or compensation.
Corvid rev B: Ninety (90) days' prior written notice.
Playbook PB-2: Standard = thirty (30) days' notice. Approved fallback: up to forty-five (45) days. Escalation: any notice period above forty-five (45) days requires CLO approval.
Assessment: The 90-day request materially exceeds both the 30-day standard and the 45-day approved fallback ceiling. It locks Customer into payments during a 90-day wind-down-like period without the protections of a negotiated wind-down.
Position: REJECT at 90 days. Counter at the standard thirty (30) days, conceding at most to the forty-five (45) day approved fallback floor only if needed to close.
Approval: CLO approval required for any figure above 45 days.

DEVIATION 5 — NEW Section 7.4 (Wind-Down): upon any termination other than for Provider's uncured material breach, a sixty (60) day wind-down applies during which Customer pays the full monthly base service fee plus all committed third-party costs.
Base (client form v2): No wind-down period and no wind-down compensation.
Corvid rev B: Adds a 60-day, full-fee wind-down plus committed third-party costs.
Playbook PB-3: A post-termination wind-down is acceptable only if (i) capped at thirty (30) days and (ii) compensation limited to documented out-of-pocket costs and non-cancelable third-party commitments. Full-fee wind-down compensation is OUT OF POLICY.
Assessment: The proposal is out of policy on both prongs: the 60-day period exceeds the 30-day cap, and full monthly-fee compensation during wind-down is full-fee compensation, which the playbook expressly prohibits. At $85,000/month, a 60-day full-fee wind-down would cost Customer $170,000 (two months) plus committed third-party costs — versus the acceptable alternative of, at most, 30 days of documented out-of-pocket and non-cancelable third-party commitments.
Position: REJECT. Counter at the playbook-acceptable wind-down: maximum thirty (30) days, compensation limited to documented out-of-pocket costs and non-cancelable third-party commitments, and no full-fee wind-down payment.
Approval: Reject to standard; no escalation needed if stated terms are held.

DEVIATION 6 — Section 9.1 (Limitation of Liability): Cap measurement period reduced from the twenty-four (24) months preceding the claim to twelve (12) months.
Base (client form v2): Cap at Fees paid or payable by Customer in the twenty-four (24) months preceding the first event giving rise to liability.
Corvid rev B: Twelve (12) months.
Playbook PB-5: Standard = twenty-four (24) month measurement period. Approved fallback floor = eighteen (18) months. A twelve (12) month measurement period is BELOW the fallback floor and requires CLO approval.
Assessment: The 12-month measurement period cuts the effective liability cap in half relative to the 24-month standard. At the current $85,000 monthly base fee this is the single largest financial deviation in the markup.
Quantified exposure (see Part IV): Standard 24-month cap = $2,040,000; approved fallback floor 18-month cap = $1,530,000; Corvid's proposed 12-month cap = $1,020,000. The counterparty's ask reduces the ceiling by $1,020,000 versus standard and by $510,000 versus the fallback floor.
Position: REJECT at 12 months. Counter at the eighteen (18) month approved fallback floor at most. The twelve-month period is below the playbook floor and should not be conceded without CLO approval.
Approval: CLO approval required for any period below 18 months.

DEVIATION 7 — Section 9.2 (Carve-Outs): deletion of clause (c), exposing gross negligence and willful misconduct to the Section 9.1 cap.
Base (client form v2): Cap does not apply to (a) Confidentiality breach, (b) IP Indemnification, or (c) gross negligence or willful misconduct.
Corvid rev B: Deletes clause (c), so gross negligence/willful misconduct are subject to the cap. Clauses (a) and (b) are retained.
Playbook PB-5: The carve-outs for confidentiality, IP indemnification, and gross negligence/willful misconduct are NON-NEGOTIABLE; deletion of any carve-out requires JOINT CLO AND CFO approval.
Assessment: Provider is attempting to cap its own gross negligence and willful misconduct liability. The playbook treats this carve-out as non-negotiable.
Position: REJECT. Restore clause (c) so that gross negligence and willful misconduct are excluded from the cap. This is a non-negotiable playbook term; retaining it avoids the need for joint approval.
Approval: If, contrary to policy, the deletion were to be accepted, joint CLO and CFO approval would be required. Recommend not accepting.

DEVIATION 8 — Section 11.2 (Service Credits): aggregate monthly service-credit cap reduced from 20% to 10% of the monthly base fee.
Base (client form v2): Aggregate cap of 20% of the monthly base service fee in any calendar month.
Corvid rev B: Aggregate cap of 10%.
Playbook PB-6: Standard = 20% aggregate monthly credit cap. Approved fallback floor = 15%. A 10% aggregate credit cap is OUT OF POLICY.
Assessment: Reducing the credit cap to 10% weakens Customer's remedy for uptime shortfalls. At $85,000/month, a 10% cap = $8,500 of maximum monthly credits versus $17,000 at the 20% standard. The 10% figure falls below the 15% playbook floor.
Position: REJECT at 10%. Counter at the fifteen percent (15%) approved fallback floor, or hold at the 20% standard.
Approval: Reject to at least the 15% floor; the 10% ask is out of policy.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
IV. TRANSFER / EXPOSURE IMPACT SUMMARY (at $85,000 monthly base fee)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
The Playbook directs escalation analyses to quantify exposure at the agreement's current monthly run-rate. The monthly base fee in the operative draft is $85,000.

A. Limitation of Liability Cap (Deviation 6)
- Standard measurement (24 months): 24 x $85,000 = $2,040,000
- Approved fallback floor (18 months): 18 x $85,000 = $1,530,000
- Counterparty ask (12 months): 12 x $85,000 = $1,020,000
- Exposure transferred away from Customer by the 12-month ask vs. standard: $1,020,000 reduction in the cap.
- Exposure transferred vs. fallback floor: $510,000 reduction.

B. Wind-Down Compensation (Deviation 5)
- 60-day full-fee wind-down: 2 months x $85,000 = $170,000, plus all committed third-party costs.
- Playbook-acceptable alternative (30 days, out-of-pocket/non-cancelable third-party only): at most $85,000 of documented out-of-pocket commitments spread differently — with no full-fee payment.
- Net averted obligatinal exposure if 60-day full-fee wind-down is rejected: up to $170,000 plus uncapped third-party pass-through.

C. Service-Credit Cap (Deviation 8)
- Standard cap 20% = $17,000/month maximum credits.
- Fallback floor 15% = $12,750/month.
- Counterparty ask 10% = $8,500/month.
- Reduction in Customer remedy potential if accepted: $8,500/month ($4,250 vs. fallback floor).

D. Late-Interest Rate (Deviation 2)
- Increment from 1.0% to 1.5% per month on late undisputed balances adds 50% to the monthly late payment cost to Customer for any period Customer is late (relevant only if Customer ever pays late; an asymmetric cost shift).

E. Renewal / Convenience / Suspension (Deviations 1, 3, 4)
- Two-year renewal commits Customer for a full additional year beyond the standard one-year period — economic and strategic lock-in.
- 90-day convenience notice vs. 30 days extends the committed payment runway by up to two months (up to $170,000 of additional committed fees) absent a negotiated wind-down counterpart.
- Suspension right (15-day cure) creates an operations-stop risk to Customer disproportionate to the underlying payment exposure.

Net Transfer Impact: The rev B markup, if accepted in full, transfers significant economic value and operational risk to Customer — most notably a halving of the liability cap (-$1,020,000 vs. standard), a 60-day full-fee wind-down (up to $170,000+), a halved service-credit remedy, a doubled convenience-notice runway, a higher late rate, a suspension lever, and a multi-year renewal lock. All eight deviations are outside the playbook Standard; five are out of policy or below the approved fallback (1, 3, 6, 7, 8); two exceed stated ceilings (2, 4); and one (5) is expressly prohibited.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
V. PARTNER (GC) INSTRUCTION COMPLIANCE AND APPROVAL REQUIREMENTS
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Per the GC engagement letter (14 July 2026) and supplemental letter (21 July 2026):
- Every rev B change must be answered by reference to the Playbook (accept / counter at approved fallback / reject) and carry specific counter figures. This report does so above.
- Out-of-policy asks (at minimum the renewal-period change and any term breaching a playbook floor) must be elevated; financial exposure must be quantified at the $85,000 monthly base fee. Quantification is provided in Part IV.
- The Deail Committee meeting has been advanced to 29 July 2026; the escalation analysis is consolidated into this deviation report serving as the basis for the board-approval package.
- Work is to be done only from the operative rev B counter-draft; rev A (withdrawn) is excluded.

Required Approvers by Deviation:
- Deviation 1 (Renewal): CLO (no fallback). Recommend reject.
- Deviation 2 (Late interest): None (reject to standard 1.0%).
- Deviation 3 (Suspension): CFO sign-off required for any suspension right; recommend reject.
- Deviation 4 (Convenience 90 days): CLO approval required above 45 days; recommend counter to 30/45.
- Deviation 5 (Wind-down): Reject to playbook-capable 30-day, OOP-only wind-down; no escalation if held.
- Deviation 6 (Cap period 12 mo): CLO approval required below 18 months; recommend counter to 18-month floor.
- Deviation 7 (Carve-out deletion): joint CLO + CFO approval; recommend reject/restore.
- Deviation 8 (Credit cap 10%): Reject; counter to 15% floor; no escalation if held.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
VI. RECOMMENDED COUNTER POSITIONS (specific figures)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Against the Corvid rev B markup, the recommended counter-redline positions are:

1. Section 2.2 Renewal — REJECT 2-yr; hold one (1) year automatic renewal periods.
2. Section 4.3 Late interest — REJECT 1.5%; hold 1.0% per month (or max lawful rate, if lower).
3. Section 4.4 (new) Suspension — REJECT; no suspension right (basis: no suspension in client form; PB-4 bars unless 30-day cure + CFO sign-off).
4. Section 7.2 Convenience — REJECT 90 days; counter at thirty (30) days (cap forty-five (45) per fallback).
5. Section 7.4 (new) Wind-down — REJECT 60-day full-fee wind-down; counter at thirty (30)-day wind-down limited to documented out-of-pocket and non-cancelable third-party commitments.
6. Section 9.1 Cap — REJECT 12-month measurement; counter at eighteen (18) months (fallback floor).
7. Section 9.2 Carve-out — REJECT deletion; restore gross negligence/willful misconduct carve-out (clause (c)).
8. Section 11.2 Credits — REJECT 10% cap; counter at fifteen percent (15%) (fallback floor) or hold at 20%.

All other terms of the client form v2 are accepted as drafted in the rev B counter-draft, and no additional deviations are identified.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
VII. CONCLUSION
---------------------------------------------------------------------
The Corvid rev B counter-draft, relative to the Northgale client-form MSA v2, introduces eight deviations, all of which fall outside the Playbook Standard and collectively transfer material economic and operational risk to Customer. None should be accepted as proposed. The recommended counter positions in Part VI keep every term at or above the approved playbook floors, with escalation required only for the renewal-period change (CLO) if any concession is contemplated. The quantified exposure at $85,000/month supports rejecting the liability-cap, wind-down, convenience-notice, and credit-cap asks outright, while countering at the playbook fallback figures.

The deviation analysis contained herein is intended to satisfy the GC's instruction for a term-by-term reconciliation of the rev B markup against the Playbook, with quantified exposure, and to serve as the substantive basis for the consolidated board-approval package due ahead of the 29 July 2026 Deal Committee meeting.
